chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir, from ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, from Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, who said:
I asked him about supererogatory prayer during the day, and he mentioned: “That eight rakʿahs are prayed before al-Ẓuhr and eight after it.”

The manner of inference from these hadiths for what we have mentioned is that every hadith narrated concerning a reduction from fifty rakʿahs only pertains to the daytime nawafil. As for the night nawafil, there is no disagreement concerning them among our companions. If these hadiths indicate the detailed explanation of what we have mentioned regarding the daytime salat, then what we intended is established. No one may say that the narration of Zurārah which you cited earlier included mention of the two rakʿahs after al-Maghrib, and that this is a disagreement regarding the night nawafil, because the narration—even if it is as he said—it is possible that he mentioned the four rakʿahs in detail, such that he said: two rakʿahs after al-Maghrib and two rakʿahs before the later ʿIshāʾ, in accordance with what was contained in the report narrated by Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, previously mentioned. These two rakʿahs, even if they are attached to the later ʿIshāʾ, are part of the nawafil of al-Maghrib, because the later ʿIshāʾ has no nafilah apart from the two rakʿahs performed sitting, which we mentioned earlier; this indicates that.

key_terms.الْخَمْسِينَ رَكْعَةً: the total count of fifty rakʿahs referred to in the legal discussion

ai.seo_question: How do Shia hadith explain the number of daytime nawafil and the total fifty rakʿahs of daily recommended prayers?
ai.summary: This text discusses the legal arrangement of the recommended daily prayers, especially the daytime nawafil surrounding al-Ẓuhr. It argues that reports mentioning fewer than fifty rakʿahs concern the daytime supererogatory prayers only, while the night nawafil remain undisputed among the Imami companions.
